To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the only patient-controlled variable associated with good glycaemic control is dietary management, and this variable is affected by the patient's level of depressive symptoms.

(1) in a Mexican population with diabetes mellitus, hyperglycaemia is significantly associated with factors that are not under patient control; (2) following a special diet reduces the likelihood of hypergylcaemia; (3) depression reduces the likelihood of following a diet and exercising, which in turn reduces the likelihood of having hyperglycaemia; and (4) depression management and dietary counselling may improve the self-management of diabetes and, therefore, glycaemic control
In this study of patients at high risk for diabetes complications, the self-management variable that had the strongest effect on glycaemic was following a special dietary regimen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relative impact of factors under patient control on hyperglycaemia in a high-risk Mexican population.
the relative effect of self management practices on glycaemia control in type 1 diabetic patients in Mexico.
the relative impact of patient self-management practices on hyperglycaemia, as well as the role of depression in self-management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative effect of selfmanagement practices on glycaemia control in type 1 diabetic patients in Mexico is not significant.
diet is an important factor in the management of diabetes in this population and is the one variable that is most amenable to change.
the relative impact of diabetes self-management activities on A1C is limited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-management practices of patients diagnosed with diabetes in Mexico, particularly dieting, are not associated with better glycaemic control.
patients in Mexico have little control over factors that affect hyperglycaemia and that depression is a significant barrier to good self-management.
the most important factor in glycaemic control was having a family member with the disease, followed by the length of time since diagnosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to improve the glycaemic control of this population, it is necessary to focus on factors that are not within their direct control, such as duration of diabetes, and those factors that are, such as diet and exercise.

, in order for self-management to have an impact on glycaemic levels, it is important to consider the effect of factors outside patient control, and also the impact that depression can have on self-management.
, for patients with diabetes in Mexico, self-management is not the main factor in achieving glycaemic control.
